name: Laguna Toro
region: Los Glaciares National Park, north sector
why: A long, quiet valley walk off the Fitz Roy crowds, to a camp by a milky lake where the Río Túnel glacier ends.
book: Registration at the park visitor centre is mandatory (the trail is unmarked). Park entry fee at El Chaltén. The camp at Laguna Toro is free and basic: bring tent, stove and food.
water: Streams along the valley; filter or treat. Nothing to buy after the village.
dangers: Unmarked in places: carry a map or GPS track.
Strong wind on the open pass above the Río Túnel valley.
River crossings swell in the afternoon and after rain.
turnaround: If you are not over the high point by 13:00, camp lower or go back: the walk in takes about 7 hours.

points.name: Los Glaciares visitor centre, El Chaltén
points.note: Register here first. The trail leaves south of the village with the Pliegue Tumbado path and then turns west.

points.name: Campamento Laguna Toro
points.note: The free camp in a lenga grove after about 16 km, with an emergency shelter. Pitch on the marked sites.

points.name: Laguna Toro and Glaciar Río Túnel
points.note: Twenty minutes past the camp: the lake shore, the glacier tongue in front, the start of the Huemul Circuit beyond.
